rashidun.title: Flag of the Rashidun Caliphate
desc:
- The Rashidun Caliphate (632–661) was the first of the four major Islamic caliphates
- Its banner was plain white, symbolising purity and the legacy of the Prophet
- **Construction:** a plain black or white field (sources vary), with no emblem. The earliest Islamic caliphate used simple monochrome banners
trivia:
- The Rashidun Caliphate (632–661) was the first Islamic state and empire
- Represented the beginning of Islamic expansionist period
- Established the foundation for Islamic civilisation

umayyad.title: Flag of the Umayyad Caliphate

colors.note: The official colour of the Umayyad Caliphate (661–750 CE).

desc: - The Umayyad Caliphate (661–750) continued the white banner tradition, representing the conquest of Mecca. Damascus served as its capital
- **Construction:** a plain white field. The Umayyad dynasty used white as their dynastic colour, in contrast to the Abbasid black
trivia:
- The Umayyad Caliphate (661–750) was the second Islamic caliphate
- Represented the peak of early Islamic expansion and power
- Conquered territories from Spain to Central Asia

abbasid.title: Flag of the Abbasid Caliphate (Black Standard)

colors.note: The official colour of the Abbasid Caliphate (750–1517 CE).

desc: - The Abbasid Caliphate (750–1258) adopted the Black Standard (al-Raya), referencing the turban of the Prophet. Baghdad was its great capital
- **Construction:** a plain black field. Black was the dynastic colour of the Abbasids, in opposition to the Umayyad white
trivia:
- The Abbasid Caliphate (750–1258) was the longest-lasting Islamic caliphate
- Ruled from Baghdad, which became one of the world's greatest cities
- Known for patronage of science, medicine, mathematics, and philosophy

fatimid.title: Flag of the Fatimid Caliphate

colors.note: The official colour of the Fatimid Caliphate (909–1171 CE); associated with the Prophet's descendants.

desc: - The Fatimid Caliphate (909–1171) used a green banner, representing the house of Ali and the Prophet's cloak. Cairo was founded as its capital
- **Construction:** a plain green field. Green was adopted as the Fatimid dynastic colour, later broadly associated with Islam
trivia:
- The Fatimid Caliphate (909–1171) ruled Egypt, North Africa, and the Levant
- Represented one of the great Islamic dynasties and centres of learning
- The green colour represented Islamic faith

ayyubid.title: Banner of the Ayyubid Dynasty
desc: - The Ayyubid Dynasty (1171–1260), founded by Saladin, carried a yellow banner adorned with an eagle — the origin of the Eagle of Saladin heraldic emblem
- **Construction:** a yellow field, sometimes with the Eagle of Saladin. The yellow colour was the dynastic standard of the Ayyubids
trivia:
- The Ayyubid dynasty (1169–1250) was founded by Saladin and ruled Egypt, Syria, and the Levant
- The plain yellow/gold flag represented the dynasty's power and Islamic faith
- The Ayyubids were famous for their military victories during the Crusades

ottoman.title: Flag of the Ottoman Empire

colors.note: Imperial Ottoman colour; represents sovereignty and military might.
The crescent and star, symbols adopted from Byzantine Constantinople.

desc:
- A red field with a white crescent and five-pointed star
- One of history's most influential flag designs, the Ottoman flag evolved over centuries
- The red field became standard by the 18th century; the crescent was associated with the Ottomans from at least the fall of Constantinople in 1453
- The Ottoman flag directly inspired the modern flags of Turkey, Tunisia, Algeria, Libya, and several other former Ottoman territories
- **Construction:** a red field with a white crescent (opening towards the fly) and a white five-pointed star between the cusps
- Various ratios were used historically
trivia:
- The Ottoman crescent and star inspired more than 15 modern national flags
- The design originated in the 14th century and became iconic for the Ottoman Empire
- The crescent and star remain the most common Islamic symbols on national flags today

ottoman-early.title: Early Ottoman Banner

colors.note: Imperial colour of the early Ottoman state.

desc: - Early Ottoman banners varied; a common form was red with a green circle and crescents, used before the standardisation of the late Ottoman flag
- **Construction:** early Ottoman banners varied but typically featured a red or green field, sometimes with calligraphic inscriptions
trivia:
- Early Ottoman flags represented the dynasty in its founding period
- Evolution of Ottoman heraldry and symbolism
- Developed into the recognisable crescent and star design

mughal.title: Flag of the Mughal Empire
desc: - The Mughal Empire (1526–1857) used green banners with gold lion-and-sun motifs. The empire ruled most of the Indian subcontinent
- **Construction:** a green field, sometimes with a lion-and-sun motif or other dynastic emblems. The Mughals used elaborate standards varying by emperor
trivia:
- The Mughal Empire (1526–1857) ruled most of the Indian subcontinent
- Represented one of history's greatest empires and centres of culture
- Known for monumental architecture including the Taj Mahal

almohad.title: Flag of the Almohad Caliphate
desc: - The Almohad Caliphate (1121–1269) ruled the Maghreb and Iberia. Its red banner featured a gold checkered square motif
- **Construction:** typically a plain red field, sometimes bearing a chequered pattern. The Almohads used red as their primary colour
trivia:
- The Almohad Caliphate (1121–1269) controlled North Africa and Al-Andalus (Islamic Spain)
- The plain crimson flag represented the dynasty's uncompromising Islamic stance
- The Almohads were famous for their military campaigns and architectural achievements

almoravid.title: Flag of the Almoravid Dynasty
desc: - The Almoravid Dynasty (1040–1147) originated in present-day Mauritania and Morocco. They used white banners in the tradition of the Umayyads
- **Construction:** a plain white field, consistent with the Almoravid preference for austere religious symbolism
trivia:
- The Almoravid dynasty (1040–1147) ruled North Africa and Spain during the early Crusades
- The flag represented Berber military power in medieval North Africa
- The Almoravids were instrumental in resisting Crusader expansion

idrisid.title: Flag of the Idrisid Dynasty
desc: - The Idrisid Dynasty (788–974) was the first Moroccan state and first Shia dynasty in the western Maghreb. They used white and green banners
- **Construction:** a plain white field with green elements. The Idrisids were among the first Moroccan dynasties
trivia:
- The Idrisid dynasty (788–974) founded the first Arab-Islamic state in the Maghreb
- The green flag represented Islamic faith
- Founded the city of Fes, a major centre of Islamic learning

samanid.title: Flag of the Samanid Empire
desc: - The Samanid Empire (819–999) was a Sunni Iranian dynasty in Central Asia. Their banners echoed the Abbasid black standard tradition
- **Construction:** a black field, following the Abbasid convention as the Samanids were Abbasid governors
trivia:
- The Samanid Empire (819–999) ruled Central Asia and parts of Iran
- Represented a golden age of Persian culture and science
- Known for patronage of scholars and poets
